# Introduction

`odytools` is an R package containing a miscellaneous collection of functions designed to make our daily work easier. Here, we focus on the most important functions related to REDCap data import and exploration.

`odytools` provides functions for very specific tasks; proper data management and reporting workflows should also include other packages typically used in data science. A great starting point to learn more about using R is [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/){.uri}. For data summaries, the [gtsummary](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/) package is highly recommended.

# Setup

## Install odytools

odytools is hosted in [GitHub](https://github.com/VHIO-Odyssey/odytools). It can be installed using the `devtools` package.

```{r}
#| label: instalation
#| eval: false

# Install devtools if you don't have it already
install.packages("devtools")

# Install odytools from GitHub
devtools::install_github("VHIO-Odyssey/odytools")

```

## Load packages

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

# Load required packages
library(odytools)
library(usethis)
library(dplyr)
library(labelled)
library(lubridate)
library(gtsummary)

```

# Import data

## API key

You need a REDCap API key to import data from a REDCap project. It is recommended to store the API key in your `.Renviron` file for security reasons. You can edit your `.Renviron` file using the `usethis` package.

```{r}
#| label: edit-renviron
#| eval: false

# This function will open your .Renviron file
edit_r_environ()

```

Values are stored as key-value pairs, one per line. For example, if your API key is `your_redcap_api_key` and want to store it under the name `MY_PROJECT`, you would add the following line to your `.Renviron` file.

`MY_PROJECT=your_redcap_api_key`

You need to restart your R session after editing your `.Renviron` file for the changes to take effect. You can access the stored API key using the `Sys.getenv()` function.

```{r}
#| label: get-api-key

# Executing this will return the value of the MY_PROJECT variable.
Sys.getenv("MY_PROJECT")

```

## Import REDCap Project

The most important function in `odytools` for importing REDCap data is `ody_rc_import()`. You just need to provide your REDCap API key as an argument.

```{r}
#| label: import-redcap
#| eval: false

# Import the REDCap data.
# See ?ody_rc_import for more details.
redcap_data <- ody_rc_import(Sys.getenv("MY_PROJECT"))

```

```{r}
#| label: load-redcap_data
#| include: false

# Trampilla para no descargarlos de nuevo cada vez
load(here::here("odytools", "redcap_data.RData"))


# Selecciona 20 casos aleatorios para agilizar los ejemplos
set.seed(556)
rnd_cases <- sample(attr(redcap_data, "subjects"), 20)

redcap_data <- ody_rc_filter_subject(redcap_data, rnd_cases)

```

# Anatomy of the imported object

## Nested structure

We'll use a test classic REDCap project with no events as an example. In this case, the imported object is a nested data frame where each row corresponds to a form.

```{r}
#| label: view-redcap-data

redcap_data

```

The key concept to understand here is "nested." The idea is that a cell in a data frame can contain another data frame. For example, the ninth element of the column `redcap_form_data` is itself a data frame containing the tumor baseline information.

```{r}
#| label: nested-structure

# Extract de ninth element of the redcap_form_data column.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[9]]

```

Also note that this is a unique form (`redcap_instance_type` is 'unique' and `redcap_instance_number` is empty). Repeating forms would have `redcap_instance_type` as 'form' and `redcap_instance_number` indicating the instance number.

```{r}
#| label: repeating-form

# Extracts the third element of the redcap_form_data column.
# It is a repeating form with multiple instances per subject.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[3]]

```

## Variables

Variables are stored in raw format as characters, exactly as they were imported from REDCap including missing data codes.

```{r}
#| label: variable-values

# Extract the 'psa_diagnosis_value' column from the ninth element of redcap_form_data.
# It contains a numeric variable.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[9]]$psa_diagnosis_value

```

```{r}
#| label: variable-values-2

# Extract the 'date_diagnosis' column from the ninth element of redcap_form_data.
# It contains a date variable.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[9]]$date_diagnosis


```

If applicable, variables are labeled according to the metadata information.

```{r}
#| label: variable-labels

# Extract the 'pt' column from the ninth element of redcap_form_data.
# It contains a labeled variable.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[9]]$pt

```

For checkbox variables (those allowing multiple selections) a label is created for each choice and present combination of choices.

```{r}
#| label: checkbox-variable-labels

# 'first_met_location' is a checkbox variable. 
# All the present combinations are labelled.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location

```

Associated with each checkbox variable is a set of binary variables (FALSE/TRUE) indicating whether each choice was selected.

```{r}
#| label: checkbox-binary-variables

# Binary variables associated with the 'first_met_location' checkbox variable.
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___1
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___2
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___3
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___4
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___5
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___6
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___7
redcap_data$redcap_form_data[[11]]$first_met_location___8


```


## Attributes

Apart from the data itself, the imported object contains several attributes with information about the project.

```{r}
#| label: redcap-attributes

# All the available attributes of the imported REDCap data.
names(attributes(redcap_data))

```

Any of these attributes can be accessed using the `attr()` base function.

```{r}
#| label: project-metadata

# Access the 'metadata' attribute.
attr(redcap_data, "metadata")

```


# Data Selection

As we have already shown, you can access the different elements of the imported REDCap data using base R code. However, `odytools` provides functions to facilitate data exploration. 

The most straightforward way to select variables from the imported REDCap data is using the `ody_rc_select()` function. You just need to provide the imported data and the variable names you want to select. If all the variables are in the same form, the function will return a data frame with the selected variables.

```{r}
#| label: rc-select

# Select the variables 'date_diagnosis' and 'pt' which are in the same form.
ody_rc_select(redcap_data, date_diagnosis, pt)

```

Note that apart from the desired variables, the function automatically includes the subject identifier and the information about the form and instance type/number.

If the variables are in different forms, the function will return a list of data frames, one per form.

```{r}
#| label: rc-select-multiple-forms

# Select the variables 'origin' and 'histology' which are in different forms.
ody_rc_select(redcap_data, origin, histology)

```

In case you want all the variables from a specific form, you can use the `ody_rc_select_form()` function. You just need to provide the imported data and the form name. 

```{r}
#| label: rc-select-form

# Select all the variables from the 'tumor_baseline' form.
ody_rc_select_form(redcap_data, tumor_baseline)

```

# Data Formatting

Although variables are labeled according to the metadata information, their actual values remain raw.

```{r}
#| label: raw-variable-values

# pT, pN and pM raw values directly extracted from the REDCap data. 
ody_rc_select(redcap_data, pt, pn, pm)


```

To format variable values according to the metadata information, you can use the `ody_rc_format()` function. It just needs a data frame with the raw variable values as input and will return a data frame with the formatted variable values.

```{r}
#| label: formatted-variable-values

# Formatted pT, pN and pM values.
# First select the variables, then pipe the result to ody_rc_format().
ody_rc_select(redcap_data, pt, pn, pm) |> 
ody_rc_format()

```

Note that after formatting, missing data codes are converted to regular missing values (`NA`). This makes sense because formatted variables are typically used for data analysis, where a missing value is just a missing value, regardless of the reason it is missing. However, if you want to keep missing data codes as they are, you can set the `keep_user_na` argument to `TRUE`.

```{r}
#| label: formatted-variable-values-keep-na

# Formatted pT, pN and pM values keeping missing data codes.
# First select the variables, then pipe the result to ody_rc_format().
ody_rc_select(redcap_data, pt, pn, pm) |> 
  ody_rc_format(keep_user_na = TRUE)


```



# Other Utilities

## Spread the data

The nested structure of the imported REDCap data is the most natural way to contain a set of forms where each one can have multiple instances per subject. However, sometimes it is more convenient to have a one-row-per-subject format. The `ody_rc_spread()` function spreads the imported REDCap data into a one-row-per-subject format. It only requires the imported data as input and returns a data frame with one row per subject. Forms with multiple instances will have their variable names suffixed with the instance number.

```{r}
#| label: rc-subsample
#| include: false

redcap_data_copy <- redcap_data

redcap_data <- redcap_data |> 
  slice(c(2, 12))

```


```{r}
#| label: rc-spread

# Spread the REDCap data to a one-row-per-subject format.
ody_rc_spread(redcap_data)

```

```{r}
#| label: rc-back
#| include: false

# Restore the original redcap_data object
redcap_data <- redcap_data_copy

```


## Filter subjects

If you are interested on working with a subset of subjects from the imported REDCap data, you can use the `ody_rc_filter_subject()` function. You just need to provide the imported data and a vector with the subject identifiers you want to keep. This will create a new object containing only the selected subjects.


```{r}
#| label: filter-subjects

# Select a subset of subjects from the imported REDCap data.
selected_subjects <- c("11685296", "14176593", "18614291")

# Filter the REDCap data to keep only the selected subjects.
redcap_data_subset <- ody_rc_filter_subject(redcap_data, selected_subjects)

# View pT, pN and pM values for the selected subjects.
ody_rc_select(redcap_data_subset, pt, pn, pm)

```

## The Data Viewer

REDCap data can be explored using the `ody_rc_view()` function. This function launches an interactive data viewer in your web browser, allowing you to explore the data in a user-friendly way. This viewer is the same as the one hosted [here](https://redcapviewer.vhio.net/). When launching the viewer locally, simply click the submit button without entering an API key; it will use the `redcap_data` object passed as an argument. Refer to [this document](https://github.com/VHIO-Odyssey/redcap_viewer/blob/master/docs/redcap_viewer_doc_20251023.pdf) for more details.

```{r}
#| label: launch-data-viewer
#| eval: false

# Launch the REDCap data viewer.
ody_rc_view(redcap_data)


```


# An Example

We are going to create a baseline summary table using data imported from REDCap. The table will include age at diagnosis, histology, PSA at diagnosis, and TNM staging. We will need data from two different forms (demographics and tumor_baseline) and make some calculations.

```{r}
#| label: example-load-data
#| include: false

load(here::here("odytools", "redcap_data.RData"))

```

```{r}

birth_date <- 
  ody_rc_select(redcap_data, birthdate) |> 
  select(-(2:4))

birth_date

baseline_raw <- 
  ody_rc_select(
    redcap_data, 
    date_diagnosis, 
    histology,
    psa_diagnosis_value,
    pt, 
    pn, 
    pm
  ) |> 
  select(-(2:4))

baseline_raw

baseline <- 
  inner_join(birth_date, baseline_raw, by = "sap") |> 
  ody_rc_format() |> 
  mutate(
    age_at_diagnosis = time_length(date_diagnosis - birthdate, "years"),
    .after = sap
  ) |> 
  select(-birthdate , -date_diagnosis)

baseline

theme_gtsummary_compact()
baseline |> 
  select(-sap) |> 
  set_variable_labels(
    histology = "Histology",
    psa_diagnosis_value = "PSA at diagnosis",
    pt = "pT",
    pn = "pN",
    pm = "pM",
    age_at_diagnosis = "Age at diagnosis (years)"
  ) |> 
  tbl_summary(
    type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
    statistic = all_continuous() ~ c(
    "{mean} ({sd})", 
    "{median} ({p25}, {p75})", 
    "{min}, {max}"
    )
  )

```

```{r}
#| label: render
#| eval: false
#| include: false
# Not evaluated chunk, execute it to render a final version of the report.
# Keep this chunk at the end of the file.
rlang::check_installed("withr")

withr::with_dir(
  rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path |> dirname(),
  quarto::quarto_render(
    input = rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path,
    output_file = odytools::ody_add_version(
      rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path |> 
        stringr::str_remove_all("^.*/|\\..*$")
    )
  )
)


```
